headline: NEW to scans -- Serbia votes today in snap parliamentary election
dek: Serbia votes today in snap parliamentary elections called by Vucic in September after almost two years of student-led anti-corruption protests triggered by the Novi Sad train-station canopy collapse (Nov 2024, 16 dead). The student-backed Students' List (professors, doctors, artists, farmers)…
sources: Reuters (Ivana Sekularac and Edward McAllister, Belgrade, Oct 25); Arab News timeline Oct 23; Al Jazeera English video explainer Oct 24
fault_line: Student revolt vs strongman record — corruption and accountability, or stability and modernisation?

sections.what_happened: Serbia votes today in snap parliamentary elections called by Vucic in September after almost two years of student-led anti-corruption protests triggered by the Novi Sad train-station canopy collapse (Nov 2024, 16 dead). The student-backed Students' List (professors, doctors, artists, farmers) seeks to end 14 years of rule by Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS); Vucic resigned the presidency on Sept 27 to run for prime minister. Polls predict a tight race. Vucic's platform: higher pensions and public salaries, health investment, youth-couple subsidies; internationally he balances closer China ties and Russia (traditional ally, main gas supplier) while leaving the EU door open. Reuters: a student victory 'would be a profound political shift' reminiscent of Orban's April defeat in Hungary and a possible blueprint for student movements elsewhere in Europe. Polls close 8 p.m. local (1900 GMT = 23:00 ); first indications expected about two hours later.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (T1) and Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA) agree on the election-day frame and the movement's origin
sections.what_disputed: Vucic remains a strong incumbent: Reuters notes many voters credit him with modernisation (highways, railways, schools, hospitals) and he accuses opponents of dividing the country. Polls are described as tight, not as a student lead.
sections.why_matters: From protest to parliament: Serbia's students try to do what the streets couldn't — unseat Vucic at the ballot box.
sections.context: Background: NEW to scans -- Serbia votes today in snap parliamentary election: student-backed Students' List vs Vucic's SNS; polls close 1900 GMT, first indications ~2h later

totw_analysis: Our read: From protest to parliament: Serbia's students try to do what the streets couldn't — unseat Vucic at the ballot box. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Student revolt vs strongman record — corruption and accountability, or stability and modernisation?
